chapter: Harry James, Bellson and the return to Duke
title: Louie Bellson and the night Duke died
summary: Louie speaks well of everyone and called Duke the Maestro; Willard saw him the night Duke died.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Willie seemed to like him very much.
Oh, yes, he was a nice guy.
And Louie. But Louie never says anything bad about anybody.
He used to call Duke the Maestro. He came by here when Duke was sick and told us, he said, 'Oh -- he was so sick,' he went to New York to see him, you know.
Yeah. He said, 'Oh, he was so sick.'

I saw him ... the night that Duke died. Basie was playing at the Palladium, and I handled the publicity for the job, and Louie came to see Basie, and he told me then, that he had been to New York to see Duke, and we were talking about Duke, and that was the night that he died.
